compiled_state.title: [cycle_dispatcher]: SHORT_CIRCUIT check is filesystem-only -> idempotency violated across CI reruns on same SHA
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## 1. Technical Environment
* Plugin Version: dso v1.17.11
* code_version: df8313c8ab4e025bafbe156577ca2ae69b095605
* Discovered during: SC10 evidence sprint (story c4f1-c18d-0000-4001, epic b575) — idempotency check on PR #270 attempt 5

## 2. Incident Overview

### Expected Behavior

Per epic b575 SC10 / story c4f1 DD: `CI re-run on same commit_sha; cycle_dispatcher SHORT_CIRCUIT; no duplicate orphan tickets/defense records/PR comments`. After the arbiter has dispatched once for a given (commit_sha), subsequent CI runs on the same SHA MUST short-circuit and not re-dispatch the arbiter or re-emit cycle markers.

### Actual Behavior

`cycle_dispatcher.next_action()` at `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/cycle_dispatcher.py:145-155` checks for SHORT_CIRCUIT via filesystem:

```python
if last_cycle and last_cycle.get("commit_sha") == current_commit_sha:
    arbiter_path = Path(artifacts) / "arbiter-rulings.json"
    if arbiter_path.exists():
        return {"action": "SHORT_CIRCUIT", ...}
```

In CI, $ARTIFACTS_DIR is ephemeral — wiped between workflow runs. So even when a prior CI attempt wrote `arbiter-rulings.json` and posted a DSO-Arbiter-Ruling PR comment, the subsequent CI re-run starts with an empty artifacts dir → `arbiter_path.exists() == False` → no SHORT_CIRCUIT → ledger reconstruction sees 4 prior cycles → next cycle = 5 ≥ max_cycles → DISPATCH_ARBITER fires again. The arbiter agent reruns. A NEW `DSO-Review-Cycle: 5` marker and `DSO-Arbiter-Ruling: 5` marker are posted.

### Empirical evidence (PR #270, attempts 4 and 5, same commit_sha=0656f88f90de34f505c122bc48518d2d021f03e9)

Before re-run (state after cycle 4):
- 4 DSO-Review-Cycle markers (cycles 1-4)
- 1 DSO-Arbiter-Ruling marker (cycle 4)

After CI re-run on same SHA (attempt 5):
- 5 DSO-Review-Cycle markers (cycles 1-5)
- 2 DSO-Arbiter-Ruling markers (cycles 4 and 5)

Expected (per SC10): 4 cycle, 1 arbiter (unchanged across reruns on same SHA).

### Root cause hypothesis

The SHORT_CIRCUIT check assumes `$ARTIFACTS_DIR` survives across cycle invocations (true locally per session; false in CI). To honor the contract in CI, the SHORT_CIRCUIT check must also consult durable storage — specifically, PR comments via `gh api .../issues/<n>/comments` looking for an existing `DSO-Arbiter-Ruling: K commit_sha=<current_sha>` marker. If found, SHORT_CIRCUIT regardless of filesystem state.

### Acceptance criteria

- `cycle_dispatcher.next_action()` must SHORT_CIRCUIT in CI when an arbiter ruling already exists on the PR for the current `commit_sha` — even when the local artifacts dir is empty.
- A regression test must drive the contract: post a DSO-Arbiter-Ruling marker for sha X, then invoke next_action with empty artifacts dir and current_sha=X → expect action=SHORT_CIRCUIT.
- After fix, re-running CI on PR #270 (or equivalent) must not add new cycle/arbiter markers.
